# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("HeermavanVoss_2024_docetaxel_millidose"))$reference`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00280-024-04684-2>
* PubMed Central: <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11420247/>

Heerma van Voss et al. gave 29 men with prostate cancer an intravenous
docetaxel test dose of 1000 ug (a "millidose") one to seven days before their
first therapeutic docetaxel infusion (75 mg/m^2 over 60 min) and asked whether
the clearance of the test dose predicts the clearance of the therapeutic dose.
The two datasets were fitted **separately** (Methods), each with a
two-compartment linear model, so the paper contributes two independent models:

* `HeermavanVoss_2024_docetaxel_millidose` --
  `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("HeermavanVoss_2024_docetaxel_millidose"))$description`
* `HeermavanVoss_2024_docetaxel_therapeutic` --
  `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("HeermavanVoss_2024_docetaxel_therapeutic"))$description`

The individual clearances of the two doses were not correlated (Spearman's
rho = 0.02, Figure 1), so the two models carry independent random effects; the
paper's conclusion is that the millidose describes docetaxel PK at the
population level (geometric mean ratio of clearance 1.44) but not in the
individual patient.

# Population

Thirty patients with prostate cancer treated with docetaxel 75 mg/m^2 as
routine care at a general hospital in the Netherlands (2017-2020, EudraCT
2016-003785-77) were enrolled; one was excluded after an allergic reaction to
the millidose, leaving 29 men (Table 1). Median age was 72 years (IQR 69-77),
mean weight 85.5 kg (95% CI 69.4-100.8), mean body-surface area 2.02 m^2
(1.79-2.23), mean creatinine 90.9 umol/L and mean bilirubin 8.8 umol/L. Serum
alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AAG) was a median 0.73 g/L on the millidose day and
0.72 g/L on the therapeutic-dose day; it was tested on clearance and not
retained. The mean therapeutic dose was 151.2 mg (133.6-168.0).

Plasma samples were drawn 0.25, 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8 h after the end of each dose
(the millidose is a bolus; the therapeutic dose a 60-min infusion). Some
therapeutic-dose samples were drawn during the infusion by mistake, and the
therapeutic-dose model gives them their own proportional residual error.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("HeermavanVoss_2024_docetaxel_millidose")()$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/HeermavanVoss_2024_docetaxel_millidose.R`
and `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/HeermavanVoss_2024_docetaxel_therapeutic.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Millidose | Therapeutic dose | Source location |
|----------------------|-----------|------------------|-----------------|
| Two-compartment linear disposition, IV input into `central` | yes | yes | Results paragraph 1 |
| `lcl` (CL at 70 kg, L/h) | log(49.6) | log(34.6) | Table 2, Clearance |
| `lvc` (Vc at 70 kg, L) | log(6.7) | log(8.00) | Table 2, Central volume (millidose printed '6,7') |
| `lq` (Q at 70 kg, L/h) | log(39.2) | log(4.63) | Table 2, Inter-compartmental clearance |
| `lvp` (Vp at 70 kg, L) | log(109) | log(22.2) | Table 2, Peripheral volume |
| `e_wt_cl` (WT/70 exponent on CL and Q) | fixed 0.75 | fixed 0.75 | Methods, allometric scaling |
| `e_wt_vc` (WT/70 exponent on Vc and Vp) | fixed 1 | fixed 1 | Methods, allometric scaling |
| `etalcl` | log(1 + 0.757^2) | log(1 + 0.617^2) | Table 2, IIV in clearance 75.7% / 61.7% |
| `etalvc` | -- | log(1 + 0.692^2) | Table 2, IIV in central volume 69.2% |
| `etalvp` | log(1 + 0.765^2) | -- | Table 2, IIV in peripheral volume 76.5% |
| `propSd` | 0.370 | 0.471 | Table 2, Residual error 37.0% / 47.1% |
| `propSd_infusion` (samples during infusion) | -- | 0.988 | Table 2, Residual error for samples drawn during infusion 98.8% |
| `Cc = central / vc * 1000` (ug/L) | yes | yes | Methods (concentrations in ug/L; Supplement GOF captions) |

# Virtual cohort

The observed data are not public. The virtual cohort draws weight and
body-surface area independently from normal distributions whose mean and
2.5th-97.5th percentiles match Table 1 (the table's "95% CI" is read as the
spread of the patients, since a confidence interval of the mean of 29 values
would be far narrower). The same 150 virtual patients receive the 1 mg
millidose in one model and 75 mg/m^2 over 1 h in the other.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20240901)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240901)

n_sub <- 150L
cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = pmax(rnorm(n_sub, mean = 85.5, sd = (100.8 - 69.4) / (2 * 1.96)), 50),
  BSA = rnorm(n_sub, mean = 2.02, sd = (2.23 - 1.79) / (2 * 1.96))
)

# Dense grid for NCA plus the paper's sampling times (0.25-8 h after the end
# of each dose; the therapeutic infusion ends at 1 h).
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.05), seq(2.25, 48, by = 0.25),
                           c(0.25, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8), 1 + c(0.25, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8))))

make_events <- function(cohort, dose_mg, tinf) {
  doses <- cohort |>
    mutate(time = 0, amt = dose_mg, evid = 1L, cmt = "central",
           rate = if (tinf > 0) amt / tinf else 0)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(cohort, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", rate = 0)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(TINF = tinf) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

ev_milli <- make_events(cohort, dose_mg = 1, tinf = 0)
ev_ther <- make_events(cohort, dose_mg = 75 * cohort$BSA, tinf = 1)

stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(unique(ev_milli[, c("id", "time", "evid")])),
  !anyDuplicated(unique(ev_ther[, c("id", "time", "evid")])),
  abs(mean(ev_ther$amt[ev_ther$evid == 1]) / 151.2 - 1) < 0.05
)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod_milli <- readModelDb("HeermavanVoss_2024_docetaxel_millidose")
mod_ther <- readModelDb("HeermavanVoss_2024_docetaxel_therapeutic")

sim_milli <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_milli, events = ev_milli, keep = "WT",
                             returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(regimen = "Millidose (1 mg bolus)")
sim_ther <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ther, events = ev_ther, keep = "WT",
                            returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(regimen = "Therapeutic (75 mg/m^2, 1 h)")
sim <- bind_rows(sim_milli, sim_ther)
```

# Typical-value check against the reported geometric-mean clearance

Table 2 gives clearance for a 70 kg patient; the Results report the geometric
mean of the individual (empirical Bayes) clearances, 57.9 L/h for the millidose
and 40.3 L/h for the therapeutic dose. Scaling the Table 2 values to the
cohort's mean weight of 85.5 kg with the fixed 0.75 exponent reproduces both,
which confirms the 70 kg reference and the allometric exponent. The ratio of
the two typical clearances is the paper's geometric mean ratio of 1.44.

```{r typical-cl}
cl70 <- c(
  millidose = exp(rxode2::rxode(mod_milli)$theta[["lcl"]]),
  therapeutic = exp(rxode2::rxode(mod_ther)$theta[["lcl"]])
)
cl_typ <- cl70 * (85.5 / 70)^0.75
tab_cl <- tibble(
  Dose = c("Millidose", "Therapeutic dose"),
  `CL at 70 kg (L/h)` = unname(cl70),
  `CL at 85.5 kg (L/h)` = unname(cl_typ),
  `Reported geometric mean (L/h)` = c(57.9, 40.3)
) |>
  mutate(`Difference (%)` = 100 * (`CL at 85.5 kg (L/h)` /
                                     `Reported geometric mean (L/h)` - 1))
knitr::kable(tab_cl, digits = 2,
             caption = "Table 2 clearance scaled to the mean weight vs. the reported geometric mean.")

stopifnot(
  all(abs(tab_cl$`Difference (%)`) < 2),
  abs(cl70[["millidose"]] / cl70[["therapeutic"]] - 1.44) < 0.02
)
```

The individual clearances of the simulated cohort centre on the same values.
Their spread includes the weight effect as well as the inter-individual
variability; the paper's geometric CVs of the empirical Bayes estimates (78.6%
and 60.7%) are shown for orientation only, since empirical Bayes estimates
shrink towards the typical value.

```{r cohort-cl}
cl_ind <- sim |>
  group_by(regimen, id) |>
  summarise(cl = first(cl), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    `Geometric mean CL (L/h)` = exp(mean(log(cl))),
    `Geometric CV (%)` = 100 * sqrt(exp(var(log(cl))) - 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(`Reported geometric mean (L/h)` = c(57.9, 40.3),
         `Reported geometric CV (%)` = c(78.6, 60.7))
knitr::kable(cl_ind, digits = 1,
             caption = "Simulated individual clearance vs. the reported empirical Bayes summaries.")

# Sampling error of a log-mean over 150 subjects with SD ~0.7 is ~6%; 20%
# leaves more than three standard errors of headroom.
stopifnot(all(abs(cl_ind$`Geometric mean CL (L/h)` /
                    cl_ind$`Reported geometric mean (L/h)` - 1) < 0.20))
```

# Concentration-time profiles

The supplement shows prediction-corrected VPCs for both datasets. The plot
below shows the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of the simulated concentrations
over the paper's 8 h sampling window (millidose) and 9 h from the start of the
infusion (therapeutic dose), for comparison with those panels. Both models
have a very fast distribution phase (initial half-life of a few minutes), so
the first sample after each dose is highly sensitive to its exact timing. The
simulated millidose median is about 7 ug/L at 0.25 h and about 1 ug/L at 1 h,
with a 95th percentile near the supplement's upper observed percentile at
0.25 h (about 20 ug/L); the observed median at 0.25 h in the prediction-
corrected VPC is lower, about 2-3 ug/L. The simulated therapeutic median is
about 1000 ug/L 15 min after the end of the infusion, falling to about
100 ug/L by 2 h.

```{r vpc, fig.height = 6}
sim |>
  filter(time > 0, time <= 9) |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after the start of dosing (h)",
       y = "Docetaxel concentration (ug/L)",
       caption = paste("Median and 90% prediction interval of 150 virtual patients;",
                       "compare the VPCs in the supplement of Heerma van Voss 2024."))
```

Dose-normalising the typical-value profiles shows how differently the two
fits distribute the drug. The therapeutic-dose model has the lower clearance
(so the larger AUC per mg), but most of that exposure falls during the
infusion; the millidose model's large, rapidly equilibrating peripheral volume
(109 L vs 22.2 L at 70 kg) keeps its dose-normalised concentration above the
therapeutic one from about 2 h onwards.

```{r typical-profiles}
typ_ev <- function(dose_mg, tinf) {
  make_events(tibble(id = 1L, WT = 85.5, BSA = 2.02), dose_mg, tinf)
}
typ <- bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_milli), events = typ_ev(1, 0),
                  returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(regimen = "Millidose (1 mg bolus)", Cn = Cc / 1),
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_ther), events = typ_ev(151.5, 1),
                  returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(regimen = "Therapeutic (151.5 mg, 1 h)", Cn = Cc / 151.5)
)
typ |>
  filter(time > 0, time <= 12) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cn, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after the start of dosing (h)",
       y = "Dose-normalised concentration (ug/L per mg)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Typical 85.5 kg patient (Table 1 mean weight and BSA).") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA. Because exposure after an intravenous dose is
`AUC = dose / CL`, the reported geometric mean clearances give a reference AUC:
1 mg / 57.9 L/h = 17.3 ug*h/L for the millidose and 151.2 mg / 40.3 L/h = 3752
ug*h/L for the mean therapeutic dose. PKNCA is run on the simulated profiles
(0-48 h, about ten terminal half-lives) and its median AUC compared with these
values.

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, regimen)
doses <- bind_rows(
  ev_milli |> filter(evid == 1) |> mutate(regimen = "Millidose (1 mg bolus)", duration = 0),
  ev_ther |> filter(evid == 1) |> mutate(regimen = "Therapeutic (75 mg/m^2, 1 h)", duration = 1)
) |>
  select(id, time, amt, regimen, duration)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | regimen + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doses, amt ~ time | regimen + id,
                             route = "intravascular", duration = "duration")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~aucinf.obs,
  "Millidose (1 mg bolus)", 1000 / 57.9,
  "Therapeutic (75 mg/m^2, 1 h)", 151.2 * 1000 / 40.3
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "regimen",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/L", tmax = "h", aucinf.obs = "ug*h/L", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = paste(
  "Simulated NCA vs. the AUC implied by the reported geometric mean clearance.",
  "* differs from reference by >20%."
))
```

The same-subject check is tighter: PKNCA's AUC for each virtual patient must
equal that patient's dose divided by their own clearance, up to the
trapezoidal and extrapolation error of the grid.

```{r auc-identity}
auc_chk <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  select(id, regimen, auc = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(sim |> group_by(regimen, id) |> summarise(cl = first(cl), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("regimen", "id")) |>
  left_join(doses |> select(id, regimen, amt), by = c("regimen", "id")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auc / (amt / cl * 1000) - 1))

auc_chk |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(`Median % difference` = median(pct_diff),
            `90th percentile of absolute % difference` = quantile(abs(pct_diff), 0.9),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "PKNCA AUC vs. dose / individual CL.")

stopifnot(
  nrow(auc_chk) == 2 * n_sub,
  abs(median(auc_chk$pct_diff)) < 2,
  quantile(abs(auc_chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 5
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports inter-individual variability in percent
  without stating the conversion. The maintainers read the percentages as
  coefficients of variation of a log-normal parameter, `omega^2 =
  log(1 + CV^2)`. The alternative reading (`omega = CV / 100`) gives about 12%
  larger standard deviations on the log scale; the paper's reported geometric
  CVs of the individual clearances (78.6% and 60.7%, which include the weight
  effect and shrinkage) do not discriminate between the two.
- **Residual error.** Table 2 percentages are used as proportional standard
  deviations (0.370, 0.471, 0.988).
- **Millidose central volume.** Table 2 prints `6,7`, read as 6.7 L (decimal
  comma).
- **Samples during the infusion.** The therapeutic-dose model applies the
  98.8% proportional error to samples taken while the infusion is running,
  detected as `tad(central) < TINF`; `TINF` must be supplied as the infusion
  duration in hours (1 h in the study). The structural model is the same for
  every sample.
- **Independent random effects across the two models.** The paper fitted the
  two datasets separately and found no correlation between the individual
  clearances (Figure 1), so the two library models carry unrelated etas. A
  simulation of the same patient under both doses (as above) draws them
  independently.
- **Virtual cohort.** Weight and BSA were drawn independently from normal
  distributions matching Table 1; the paper does not report their correlation
  or height. Age, creatinine, bilirubin and AAG do not enter either model.
- **Reference AUC.** The paper reports no NCA; the reference AUC in the
  comparison table is dose / reported geometric mean clearance, not a
  measured value.
- No correction notice affecting the model was found as of 2026-10-30 (the
  2024-08-31 revision corrected an author's name only).
